title: Canonical normalization comparing the two completed exchange presentations
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l, with the adic coefficient datum d = (O_E,(varpi)) in the published lifted coefficient presentation [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. For any chosen Cartesian square (g-prime,f-prime,f,g) of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and intrinsically complete K on X, compare the completed adjunction-mate exchange of [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange], with the square transposed by [def-sf-chosen-cartesian-square-transpose], to the ordered strict-tower exchange [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map]. The former is precisely sourceTransport.hom followed by completed pullback of pushComparison.hom, then the ordered exchange, then direct image of targetTransport.inv, then pushComparison.inv. Here sourceTransport and targetTransport are the fixed resolving-counit normalized cbcDatumCompletedTransport of [def-sf-completed-pullback-presentation-transport], and pushComparison is eqToIso of equality of the coefficient maps proved there. Thus the comparison specifies the actual arrows, not merely isomorphic endpoints. No properness, smoothness, noetherianity, dimension bound, constructibility or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: The completed coefficient structure maps agree after all finite quotient projections by def-sf-completed-pullback-presentation-transport. Consequently direct image has the eqToIso comparison displayed in the Lean statement. The universal resolving-counit normalizations identify the two ordinary pullback presentations, and identify their adjunctions and tensor-balanced square comparisons. Taking their ordinary unit-square-counit mates identifies ordinary exchange, with the direct-image comparisons at both ends.

Precompose the desired equality by the ordinary-to-completed unit at the direct image of K. The completed mate extends the ordinary mate along that unit. Apply the unit equation of the canonical completed presentation transport and naturality of the direct-image comparison. The ordered exchange unit identity gives exactly the same ordinary mate followed by the target completion unit on the other side.

Completed pullback and direct image preserve intrinsic completeness, so the common target is complete. The injective part of the completion reflector Hom bijection cancels the source unit. This proves equality of the specified maps without asserting faithfulness of finite reduction. The construction and cancellation include zero objects and empty schemes.

theorem sfCompletedExchange_transport (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare g' f' f g) (K : PbcComplete l E X) :
    let pushComparison := fun {V W : Scheme.{u}} (q : V ⟶ W) ↦
      eqToIso (congrArg (proEtaleRingDerivedDirectImage q
        (pbcAdicCompletion W (pbcIntegralDatum l E))
        (pbcAdicCompletion V (pbcIntegralDatum l E)))
        (Iso.ext (cbcDatumCoefficient_eq (pbcIntegralDatum l E) q)))
    ((sbcExchangeApp l E (exchangeTransposeSquare sq) K).hom =
        (cbcDatumCompletedTransport (pbcIntegralDatum l E) g).hom.app
            ((sbcPush l E f).obj K).obj ≫
          ((pbcIntegralDatum l E).completedPull g).map
            ((pushComparison f).hom.app K.obj) ≫
          (pbcIntegralDatum l E).completedExchange sq K.obj ≫
          ((pbcIntegralDatum l E).push f').map
            ((cbcDatumCompletedTransport (pbcIntegralDatum l E) g').inv.app K.obj) ≫
          (pushComparison f').inv.app ((sbcPull l E g').obj K).obj)
